q: 没有索引时，按 email 在百万行的表里找一个用户，为什么慢？
options: 数据库锁竞争太激烈，读写互相阻塞
SQL 解析和优化器耗时太长
无索引只能逐页扫描整张表，每页都要读盘检查
网络往返次数太多，客户端反复请求
why: 无索引时数据库别无选择，只能把每一页数据依次读进内存逐行检查；上百万页就是上百万次相对缓慢的磁盘读，只为找一条记录。
why_en: Without an index the database must sequentially scan every page, loading each from disk into memory, which means millions of slow disk reads to find one record.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Query email"] --> B["Full table scan"]
  B --> C["Check every row"]
  C --> D["Return match"]
options_en: Lock contention is too severe, blocking reads and writes against each other.
SQL parsing and query planning take too long.
Without an index it must scan every page sequentially, reading each into memory to check.
There are too many network round trips between client and server.

q: 主表数据在磁盘上的典型存储形式是？
options: 堆文件（heap file）：行按写入顺序堆放，没有特定排序
始终按主键排序的有序文件，写入需保持位置
哈希桶数组，按哈希值分散存放
列式压缩块，按列而非按行存储
why: 主表数据通常存成堆文件——行按写入先后堆放、没有特定顺序，就像来一条记一条的笔记本。这正是需要索引提供有序访问路径的原因。
why_en: Table data is typically stored as a heap file, an unordered collection of rows written as they come, which is why indexes are needed for fast lookups.
options_en: A heap file: rows stored in the order they were written, with no particular sort order.
A file always kept sorted by primary key, so writes must preserve row position.
An array of hash buckets, scattering rows by hash value.
Column-compressed blocks, storing data by column rather than by row.

q: 为什么每次数据库查询都绕不开「从磁盘加载到内存」这一步？
options: 因为内存里放不下任何数据，只能常驻磁盘
数据落在磁盘上，只有搬进内存（RAM）才能被 CPU 处理
因为磁盘硬件本身不支持随机读取
为了保证事务的隔离性级别达标
why: 数据落在磁盘（如今多为 SSD），而 CPU 只能处理内存里的数据，所以每个查询都要把相关页从磁盘搬进 RAM。索引的价值就是减少要搬的页数。
why_en: Data lives on disk but can only be processed in memory, so every query loads pages from disk into RAM, and indexes minimize how many pages that takes.
options_en: Because memory cannot hold any data at all, so everything must stay on disk.
Data lives on disk and can only be processed once it is loaded into memory (RAM).
Because the disk hardware itself does not support random reads.
To guarantee the transaction isolation level is met.

options: SSD 上两者速度完全一样，没有差距

why_en: Even on SSDs random access is still significantly slower than sequential access, a smaller gap than on HDDs but a very real one.
options_en: On SSDs the two have exactly the same speed, no gap at all.

q: 索引让查询变快的本质机制是什么？
options: 把所有数据压缩得更小，省磁盘空间
提供结构化路径，直接指出数据在哪些页，减少要读的页数
把整张表常驻内存，不必碰磁盘
并行扫描所有磁盘页，多线程加速
why: 索引是为搜索优化的独立数据结构：它告诉你目标数据具体在哪些页，从而不必逐页检查。就像用书的目录直接翻到相关页，而不是一页页找。
why_en: An index is a separate search-optimized structure that tells the database exactly which pages hold the target data, minimizing pages read from storage.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: It compresses all the data to make it smaller, saving disk space.
It provides a structured path pointing directly to the pages holding the target data, reducing pages read.
It keeps the entire table resident in memory, never touching disk.
It scans all disk pages in parallel with multiple threads.

q: 索引不是免费的。它的代价包括哪些？（多选）
options: 额外磁盘空间，有时接近原始数据大小
每次插入/更新除了改主表，还要更新表上的每一个索引
多个索引会让一次写操作触发多次磁盘写
有索引后读取一定变慢
why: 索引的三重代价：占磁盘空间、写入时每个索引都要维护、多索引放大写开销。读取恰恰是索引加速的对象，不会因此变慢。
why_en: Indexes cost extra disk space and slow down writes because every insert or update must also update each index, turning one write into several disk writes.
options_en: It costs extra disk space, sometimes nearly as much as the original data.
Every insert or update must update the main table plus every index on it.
Multiple indexes turn a single write into several disk writes.
Reads always get slower once you add an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时同步更新索引结构的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index maintenance is the overhead of keeping index structures updated on every write.

q: 对这张表，关于索引的正确判断是？
options: 尽量多建索引以防万一，覆盖所有可能查询
必须建覆盖索引，避免任何回表

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库管理员，负责数据库运维和优化的角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DBA stands for Database Administrator, the role responsible for operating and tuning databases.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.
